rejected_rule.statement: A person's continued possession of a property for over ten years, without payment of rent or produce, or performance of service or duty, can be accepted as proof of undisturbed and uninterrupted possession by a title adverse to or independent of that of the Plaintiff, unaccompanied by any act by the possessor that would fairly and naturally be inferred as an acknowledgement of a right existing in another person.
rejected_rule.supporting_quote: In view of the multiple reasons set out above in detail, I am of the considered view that the substituted Defendant has satisfied the trial Court that her continued possession of the corpus since 1979, qualifies to be accepted as proof of undisturbed and uninterrupted possession by a defendant by a title adverse to or independent of that of the Plaintiff, unaccompanied by payment of rent or produce, or performance of service or duty or by any other act by the possessor, from which an acknowledgement of a right existing in another person would fairly and naturally be inferred, in terms of Section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance.
